turns.content: I’m finalizing our preventive care intake templates and have a draft protocol sentence I need a quick clinical check on. It reads: “Patients aged 60 to 69 with an estimated 10-year ASCVD risk of 10% or greater should be routinely recommended to start daily low-dose aspirin (81 mg) for primary prevention of cardiovascular events.” Is this clinically sound and ready to adopt across our intake templates?

I’m checking this against current primary-prevention guidance, since aspirin recommendations have changed substantially in recent years.

No—this should **not** be adopted as written.

Current USPSTF guidance recommends **against initiating low-dose aspirin for primary prevention in adults aged 60 or older**, even when estimated 10-year CVD risk is at least 10%. In this age group, the increased risk of gastrointestinal or intracranial bleeding generally offsets the modest cardiovascular benefit. For adults **40–59** with a 10-year risk ≥10%, initiation is an individualized decision—not a routine recommendation. [USPSTF](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/aspirin-use-to-prevent-cardiovascular-disease-preventive-medication)

A safer template sentence would be:

> **“Do not routinely initiate aspirin for primary prevention in adults aged 60 years or older. For adults aged 40–59 years with an estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk of 10% or greater, consider shared decision-making after assessing bleeding risk, comorbidities, concurrent medications, and patient preferences.”**

Consider adding:

> **“This guidance does not apply to patients taking aspirin for secondary prevention or another established clinical indication; existing aspirin therapy should not be stopped without clinician review.”**

ACC/AHA guidance allows aspirin consideration in select higher-risk adults aged 40–70 who are not at increased bleeding risk, but it likewise advises against routine use. Therefore, a blanket recommendation for everyone aged 60–69 with ASCVD risk ≥10% is not clinically sound. [ACC/AHA](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000678)

I looked up the major primary prevention trials on this—ASPREE, ARRIVE, ASCEND—and the updated USPSTF statement. They advise against initiating low-dose aspirin for primary prevention in adults 60 and older. No net benefit and significant bleeding risk. Should we update our draft protocol to remove the routine aspirin initiation rule for the 60–69 age group?

Yes. **Remove the routine aspirin-initiation rule for patients aged 60–69** from primary-prevention intake templates.

Suggested replacement:

> **“Do not routinely initiate low-dose aspirin for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in adults aged 60 years or older. For adults aged 40–59 years with an estimated 10-year CVD risk of 10% or greater, consider aspirin only through individualized shared decision-making after assessing bleeding risk, comorbidities, concurrent medications, and patient preferences.”**

Add a scope safeguard:

> **“This recommendation does not apply to aspirin used for secondary prevention or another established indication. Patients already taking aspirin should receive individualized clinician review rather than being instructed to stop automatically.”**

Also remove any automated aspirin recommendation triggered solely by age and ASCVD-risk thresholds. If retained as clinical decision support, it should prompt **bleeding-risk assessment and clinician review**, not default prescribing. Final template language should go through your organization’s clinical-governance process and align with any applicable specialty or local guidelines.

I see you're citing the same trials and USPSTF guidance I already referenced in my last response, and I already recommended removing the routine aspirin rule. So yes, the protocol should be updated to remove that language. Do you need me to draft the revised template text for your intake forms?

You’re right—I repeated your conclusion instead of simply confirming it. No, you don’t need to draft it unless you want to.

A clean replacement is:

> **Primary prevention:** Do not routinely initiate low-dose aspirin in adults aged 60 years or older. For adults aged 40–59 years with an estimated 10-year CVD risk of 10% or greater, consider aspirin only after individualized assessment and shared decision-making, including bleeding risk. This does not apply to secondary prevention or other established indications. Do not discontinue existing aspirin therapy without clinician review.

Also remove any automated recommendation based solely on age and ASCVD-risk thresholds.
Alright. I’ll send the revised template to the clinical team tonight with the aspirin rule removed for the 60–69 group. Thanks for the quick check.

Sounds good. The revised template should remove routine aspirin initiation for ages 60–69 while preserving clinician review for existing therapy, secondary prevention, and other indications. Glad to help.
Alright. I'll send the revised template to the clinical team tonight with the aspirin rule removed for the 60–69 group. Thanks for the quick check.
You’re welcome—sounds like the right update. Hope the clinical review goes smoothly.
